notes: USD per unit for bought items. Made items have no price of their own: their cost comes from bom/materials.json. Path says how the item is obtained: buy_retail (retail or marketplace price), buy_bulk (distributor bulk price), buy_used, buy_service (fabrication service), make (computed from materials), owned or salvage. Placeholders are guesses that count in totals and are flagged. Unpriced items count as $0. Re-check every price at the seller before buying.

items.name: Holybro Pix32 v6 autopilot (new)
items.note: Holybro regular price $201.56, Holybro offer range $146.99 to $210.96, Unmanned RC $262.99 with tax.

items.name: Holybro Pix32 v5 (used, tested)
items.note: One used listing. Crash and flight history unknown. Holybro lists the v5 as discontinued.

items.name: Holybro M9N GPS for the autopilot
items.note: Holybro points to a newer V2 model. The 3DR version with compass is $74.90.

items.name: T-Motor V2207 V2 brushless motor (one of four)
items.note: T-Motor lists $13.50. Budget 2207 listings on eBay run about $10 to $27, so the low end is from unknown-quality sellers.

items.name: 4-in-1 ESC, 30 to 45 A class
items.note: Not priced. A single 40 A ESC was $13.82 at Walmart (old listing), so four separate ESCs would cost about $55. Guess only.

items.name: 5-inch propeller set
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: Commercial 5-inch frame
items.note: Not priced. Replaced by a printed frame in pass 2. Guess only.

items.name: Printed frame (PETG), from materials
items.note: Assumes 150 g of PETG, plus 20 percent waste on the high end. The PETG price is a placeholder until searched. Measure the real grams in the slicer.

items.name: Printed prop guards (set of four), from materials
items.note: Assumes 30 g of PETG for four guards. Estimate.

items.name: Printed camera mount, from materials
items.note: Assumes 30 g of PLA. Estimate.

items.name: Printed tag enclosure, from materials
items.note: Assumes 25 g of PLA for the tag case. Estimate.

items.name: Raspberry Pi 5, 4 GB (companion computer)
items.note: Raspberry Pi's post gives $70 for the 4 GB model after memory price rises. Most retailers show about $110. Check which one applies.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (video streamer or light companion)
items.note: Launch price $15. Current retailers $19 to $20.75. Supply reports conflict. Needs a mini CSI camera cable, which is not priced.

items.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 (standard lens)
items.note: Official $25. Adafruit and PiShop list $29.25. The wide lens is about $35 to $38.50.

items.name: VL53L1X time-of-flight breakout (close range)
items.note: Low is an M5Stack Grove module, not a bare breakout. High is the Pimoroni board at RobotShop. Dropped in pass 1 until logs show a need.

items.name: 4S 1500 mAh LiPo (one pack)
items.note: Use a known brand for flight. Cheap unbranded packs are a fire risk. Some 15.2 V HV packs need a matching charger and ESC. Cell-level DIY packs are not priced and are not recommended until someone experienced reviews the build.

items.name: 4S balance charger
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: LiPo charging and storage bag
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz nano receiver (manual override link)
items.note: Low is a RadioMaster XR2 Nano. High is an unbranded nano at Walmart. It needs a transmitter, and the kill path is only trusted after bench tests.

items.name: ExpressLRS-compatible transmitter (radio)
items.note: Not priced in research. Owning one already makes this $0. Guess only.

items.name: Heltec HT-CT62 (ESP32-C3 plus SX1262 LoRa node), retail
items.note: Heltec's store lists $6.90 and odlstore $9.00. A bulk ESP32-C3 module is $2 to $3.50 (see chip_esp32c3_mini1). Check the frequency variant for your region (915 MHz in the US) before buying.

items.name: NEO-M9N-00B bare GNSS module (tag)
items.note: Symmetry lists $10.99 for ten units and $15.68 for one. LCSC lists $16.04. Needs a breakout or carrier board. DigiKey reported a long lead time. This is the largest chip in the tag.

items.name: GNSS antenna and carrier board (tag, retail)
items.note: Not priced. The bare module needs an antenna and a carrier. Replaced by a board of the owner's own design in pass 7 (unverified). Guess only.

items.name: Tag battery and charge board
items.note: Not priced. Guess only.

items.name: ESP32-C3-MINI-1 module (bulk, distributor)
items.note: LCSC single pieces $2.93 to $3.53, and $2.01 to $2.59 at the 1,300-piece tier. DigiKey lists the -1U-H4 at $3.50. The -N4 and -H4 variants have a PCB antenna. Its Wi-Fi can link the tag to the drone, which replaces the LoRa chip in the retail module.

items.name: 2-layer PCB, 10 x 10 cm, one board (outsourced, low-markup fab)
items.note: The homepage lists 5 boards from $2.00 for 1 to 2 layers up to 100 x 100 mm. One user reported $3.50 for five including shipping, so $0.40 to $0.70 per board. Only one fab is listed, so this is a single-source buy until a second fab is added.

items.name: Passives and connectors for the tag (bulk)
items.note: Resistors, capacitors and a battery connector, bought in bulk. Not searched. Estimate only.

items.name: GNSS patch antenna on a 2-layer board (own design, unverified)
items.note: Unverified design: a GNSS patch on a 10 x 10 cm 2-layer board, priced as the bare board. Patch size and tuning are not checked. The u.FL connector is not priced. Measure the satellite signal (C/N0) on the M9N before trusting it.

items.name: Tag board etched in-house, 100 cm2, single-sided (comparison)
items.note: Single-sided only, for comparison with the outsourced 2-layer board. The etchant figure is conservative because ferric chloride can be reused. Per board this costs more than an outsourced 2-layer board, so in-house etching is for fast iteration, not savings.

items.name: Phone with GNSS, IMU and Wi-Fi (already owned)
items.note: Counted at $0 because you already own it. A new phone is not in the budget.

items.name: Google Pixel 8a, used (purchased by the owner)
items.note: Bought used for $250. Most spec sheets give 188 g. Its battery is a fire and crash hazard on a drone, so mount it safely and limit its charge. This is a purchase, not a free owned device, and it is far more than the Pi and camera it can replace.

items.name: USB-to-serial adapter (phone to autopilot link)
items.note: Not priced. Guess only. Needs an OTG cable if the phone is the link.

items.name: DJI Tello, refurbished (indoor bench test platform)
items.note: Optional. Indoors only, no GPS. Only for testing follow logic on a real airframe indoors, never outdoors near people. This is refurbished or open-box stock. No current new list price was found.

items.name: Thrust stand for motor tests (printed base, arm and mount)
items.note: Assumes 80 g of PLA. Pair with the load cell below. Measure real thrust before trusting any motor result.

items.name: 1 kg load cell with HX711 amplifier (set)
items.note: Walmart shows a 1 kg kit at $8.19 and four sets at about $2.80 each. A multi-capacity eBay combo was $10.59 to $13.24. Check the listing's capacity: a Walmart four-pack result was a 50 kg kit.

items.name: DIY outrunner motor, 2207 class (one of four), from materials
items.note: Per motor: 40 g of 0.3 mm wire, 14 N52 discs, two bearings, one shaft, one steel stator core, and a 30 g printed bell. The steel core is unpriced, so this total is incomplete. A DIY motor is a dependence and learning project, not a cost saving at this size.

items.name: Desktop CNC mill, 3018 class (PCB milling, capital)
items.note: Basic 3018-class kits were found at about $115 to $200. The Amazon listing showed $122 in one place and $171 in another, so check the live price. Capital cost, so optional. FAU or IEEE may already have one.

items.name: ICM-42688-P IMU chip (for a future in-house flight controller)
items.note: DigiKey single piece $4.86 and 5,000-piece reel $3.07. LCSC quotes about $20.50 for a single piece, so buy from a distributor's reel tier. Optional: not in any pass yet.

items.name: STM32H743VIT6 MCU (for a future in-house flight controller)
items.note: LCSC single piece $11.49, and about $8.11 to $8.38 at 100 pieces. The listing is undated and copies disagree. Optional: not in any pass yet.

items.name: AM32-supported ESC microcontroller (for a future in-house ESC)
items.note: AM32 lists STM32F051, STM32G071, GD32E230, AT32F415, AT32F421 and STSPIN32F0 as supported. Not priced. The ESC power stage (MOSFETs and gate driver) is also not priced.

items.name: Wearable IMU board (per unit, for later companion tiers)
items.note: Not priced. Only needed if the tiers reach wearable IMUs. Costs add up quickly per unit.
